analysis.title: GS Basics - Pivotal. Rates Resilient. Heavy Tech Selling.
key_insights: Futures sharply higher on 19 Nov, driven by NDX. US absorbed plenty of bad news the day before, but Asia was struggling.

TSMC-exposed basket down 8% and Asian data center names under pressure. New BIS rules tighten advanced AI chip licensing across parts of Asia and Brazil and restrict offshore compute access for Chinese customers. The note cites delayed projects, displaced demand and excess infrastructure capacity as effects that are hard to quantify and were not fully priced in Asia.

Offsetting the BIS hit is positioning: two months of aggressive selling have left valuations depressed across global semis. The note says it does not take much good news to squeeze, and that if the BIS implications can be compartmentalized in the Asian supply chain, that is encouraging.
Bonds rallied despite a hawkish Waller, the Fed minutes and ECB regulatory noise. The back end was well bid, the curve bull flattened and the front end was broadly unchanged.
Australia's jobs report was a big miss. The 2yr rallied hard and cuts are starting to be priced, which the note reads as potentially signaling the end of the hiking cycle.

The market is increasingly pricing weaker growth as capex expectations fall, commodities roll over and inflationary pressure fades. The note sees parallels to end-2018: the same late-cycle slowdown with very different policy implications.
Rate price action was encouraging and suggests a lot of policy is already in the price. Equity market internals are very defensive and commodities now point the same way.

Gold and precious metals face competition from a strong dollar, elevated real rates and attractive all-in credit yields. The note calls it a spending glut rather than a savings glut, a less supportive backdrop for precious metals and multiples while the Fed is tightening.
China is another headwind: weak growth, Shanghai equities near their lows and little sign of recovery. Potential restrictions on AI/data center investment add to it.

Copper has become a proxy for the AI infrastructure theme, so its resilience is hard to reconcile with collapsing AI infrastructure equities. Physical inventories, regional premiums and Chinese stockpiling are cited as nuances, but the broad commodity weakness is called striking. Precious and industrial metals, grains, gasoline and diesel are all under pressure.
The note says the broad disinflationary impulse could materially change the rates narrative.

Risk: SPX is precariously holding its 200-day moving average. Street gamma positioning is meant to be very short, but vol was soggy the previous day for the first time in a while, particularly after VIX expiry. With VIX in the mid 20s and Thanksgiving the following week, the note sees a meaningful potential tailwind if the market stabilizes.

The note argues that a lot of the AI issues are already reflected in price. If rates cooperate, it sees a legitimate bull case for equities, and says the market changed when the Fed changed its posture and may end the same way.
Today's calendar: Walmart earnings, jobless claims, Philly Fed and the 10yr TIPS auction at 18:00. Watch JPY approaching 160 and broader tech.
